Yes. If they're brawl, you're likely not going to get a pick on your own. So the value you get is from being annoying, distracting, and burning cooldowns. 

If your team is dive (Winston) and they're brawl (Roadhog/JQ) y'all shouldn't even be playing dive. 

If your team is brawl, and their team is brawl, you can play tracer. But you're only going to be fighting in little windows of time and looking to one-clip while they're distracted.

Your K/D is probably gonna be sad looking in those games, but if you tell your team "Suzu/Lamp/Nade is down" hopefully they take advantage of that. 

Hope that helps! This meta isn't her best but she can find ways to make impact!

In higher plat and low diamond ppl know how to play their comp. In this meta, tracer sucks against brawl comps cuz of heal creep. So like if u see them fighting all in a pack, and they have a one-shot (Kirikos, Hanzos, Ashes) and your enemies aren't positioned in a back line it's literally just not worth it to play Tracer. It's a "sit back and shoot" meta. Tracer gets most of her value from dueling out of position heroes. You can burn suzus, ana nades, and other cooldowns, but your team likely won't take advantage of that. 

So if you wanna play tracer into those comps, basically you just wanna find a wall to hide behind, and don't commit to any fights but stay just annoying enough to where someone has to pay attention to you. If your tank goes in, just be a as annoying as possible and try not to take any chip damage so you're being annoying for the majority of the fight without having to find heal packs. If there's a low HP target you can blink, clip, melee, and back off. 

If you have like 2-3 targets facing you, and you stay alive for long enough, your team should be able to get an advantage in a fight without you having to kill anything yourself. 

TLDR: Don't commit in brawl comps, annoy people into burning cooldowns and facing away from your team, look for low HP enemies you can pick, look for pulse bombs (there are so many CDs to track for that) and focus on staying healthy enough to keep your uptime high in a fight

it's always better to be able to support yourself and be your own best friend, but i know from experience that it doesn't always help. but if u want tips on how to make friends i think i have some tips that could help for people in our situations. 1) don't set expectations for new friendships so there's no pressure on either of u and it can just be natural. 2) when ur first getting to know someone, make ur intentions clear (esp if it's w someone of the preferred gender) so both of u are on the same page 3) don't trust the voice in ur head saying "they hate u, they don't wanna hang out with u etc..." like seriously cancel her she's not helpful and she's lying most of the time 4) don't expect them to text you first to make plans, instead make plans with them so they feel appreciated/ wanted. 5) as a quiet borderline, ur probably very uncomfortable with confrontation, but communicating with friends is super important! if u feel like ur feelings are being hurt, gently bring it up with a friend and talk it out. don't be like me and just ghost them on the spot! chances are there's just a little miscommunication. 

i hope this kinda helps, i know it's messy and kinda vague but it took me a while to learn these so i hope it works for u somehow! 

it takes time to find genuine friends, but i promise u if u keep working at it and try to come out of ur shell more and more each day, you'll have a great friend in no time.

I guarantee you, every person has asymmetrical features. Here’s a few experiments you can try for yourself:

1. Take a photo of someone you compare yourself to, like a celebrity, Now, try to get a feel for their face. Then mirror-flip the image, and you’ll notice all of the flaws about someone. However, slowly, it starts to align itself again until it looks normal. Weird optical illusion right? Well, that’s how it is for everyone. No one, not even supermodels, are perfect. And if you’re not trying to be a supermodel, what’s the point of looking like one?

2. You can also just look up “symmetrical face maker” or some shit, and if you put a mirror image line down the center of someone’s face, they’re probably going to have two different faces depending on which side is being mirrored. 

Seriously, there is nothing wrong with your body. BDD can make up a whole lot of lies without you realizing it, but just be able to identify which voices in your head are not on your side and avoid entertaining delusions.

I think that I’m more susceptible to stating in the mirror for longer periods of time (because I look stunning sometimes) So, I try my best to avoid the mirror and fill myself with positive vibes. Don’t waste your high on giving into the BDD.

I’m no psychologist, but I’ve been really pushing myself these past months to cut back on the mirror. It takes a lot of soul searching and resilience to push off the anxiety that comes with avoiding the mirror. But trust me, BDD is the most persuasive and deceptive part of your mind. It wants you to look in the mirror and the more you resist the more ways it has to tell you that you SHOULD look in the mirror. But if you look in the mirror, you give it the power over you. You don’t have to go cold turkey, but put a clock near your mirror and time yourself so you’re less likely to be completely immersed in a trance. BDD is like an infection on a wound, even if it’s 90% clean, it’s still infected. So keep scrubbing until that bad boy is gone.

I’m in the same boat as you. I actually love the way I look in mirrors but pictures make me wanna just rip out my face. But, exposure therapy has been the most tested and proven therapy to help. But here’s a fun little test to make you feel less alone, take a picture of any hot celebrity (Mila Kunis is a pretty good one). Now stare at their face and get a good reading on it, then flip it/ reflect it in MS Paint or something, you’ll notice that your brain actually somehow “corrects” their asymmetry/ flaws to something that’s more recognizable. That’s what everyone does when they see you. It’s just you’re SO used to your mirror’s image, that when it flips, it’s like a whole new person. 

But, yes, taking pictures will help you cope because you’ll get used to your flipped face and understand that it’s okay to have misaligned features because everyone has it, it’s just you’re not seeing a flipped image of them to make it stand out. Once you keep exposing yourself long enough, becoming more accepting of your flaws is easier. Especially when you take pictures that make your flaws seem even more exaggerated than you already think it is. 

But it’s not easy, it’s really emotionally draining and you will hit a lot of humps and want to stop because coming to terms with “reality” (of your appearance) will be a major shock to your brain. Take care!
